proposed_comments.title: Implement the Rich Text WinRT interop message accessor
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The declarations and call are in the diff, but the required Constants.cpp implementation and shared constant are absent from the PR.
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:** `src/common/interop/Constants.idl`, `src/common/interop/Constants.h`, `src/common/interop/Constants.cpp`, `src/common/interop/shared_constants.h`, and the Rich Text dispatch in `src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPasteXAML/App.xaml.cs`.

**Problem:** The PR declares `AdvancedPasteRichTextMessage()` in the WinRT interop interface and calls it from Advanced Paste, but the current head does not implement that accessor in `Constants.cpp` or define the corresponding shared message constant. This leaves the generated factory method with no native symbol to link against.

**Why it matters:** The focused Advanced Paste unit-test project currently fails to build with `LNK2019` for `winrt::PowerToys::Interop::implementation::Constants::AdvancedPasteRichTextMessage`. The PR is therefore not buildable as submitted.

**Suggested change:**
1. Define `ADVANCED_PASTE_RICH_TEXT_MESSAGE` as `L"PasteRichText"` in `shared_constants.h`.
2. Add `Constants::AdvancedPasteRichTextMessage()` in `Constants.cpp` returning that shared constant.
3. Append the new message alongside the existing Advanced Paste messages without changing their names.

**Verification:** Rebuild `src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste.UnitTests/AdvancedPaste.UnitTests.csproj` for `Debug|x64` and confirm the `PowerToys.Interop.vcxproj` link step no longer reports the missing symbol.

confidence.rationale: The exact current head reproducibly fails to link because the declared and called accessor has no implementation.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve existing Advanced Paste format IDs
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve existing Advanced Paste format IDs

**Severity:** `high`

`PasteFormats` values are emitted by Advanced Paste telemetry and can also affect persisted and action-ordering assumptions. The current head assigns `RichText = 11` while shifting existing values such as `ImageToText` and omitting the existing `FixSpellingAndGrammar` member, so historical and new telemetry can interpret the same numeric value as different actions.

Please restore every existing enum member and numeric value, then assign only Rich Text a new unused value. Keep visual ordering separate in the display-order helper instead of renumbering the compatibility-sensitive enum.

confidence.rationale: The current diff visibly shifts and removes telemetry-backed enum values.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve a plain-text fallback in the Rich Text clipboard package
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The correction requires coordinated changes to the data-package helper, transform call site, and focused tests.
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:** `src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste/Helpers/DataPackageHelpers.cs`, `src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste/Helpers/TransformHelpers.cs`, and `src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste.UnitTests/ServicesTests/RichTextHelperTests.cs`.

**Problem:** `CreateFromHtml()` currently puts only `StandardDataFormats.Html` on the replacement clipboard package. Because Advanced Paste replaces the system clipboard before sending paste, applications that choose plain text instead of HTML receive no readable fallback, and later text-based paste actions may no longer see a supported `Text` format.

**Why it matters:** Rich Text paste should degrade gracefully in targets that do not accept HTML. Without a text fallback, users can get an empty paste or lose the original readable Markdown or plain-text representation.

**Suggested change:**
1. Change `CreateFromHtml` to accept both generated HTML and an explicit plain-text fallback.
2. Call both `SetHtmlFormat(HtmlFormatHelper.CreateHtmlFormat(html))` and `SetText(plainText)`.
3. Update `TransformHelpers.ToRichTextAsync` to read the original clipboard text before generating HTML.
4. Update the Rich Text test to exercise `TransformHelpers.TransformAsync(PasteFormats.RichText, ...)` and assert both formats.

**Verification:** Build `AdvancedPaste.UnitTests.csproj` for `Debug|x64`, run the Rich Text test, and verify the HTML fragment contains the expected markup while the text fallback remains readable and contains no HTML tags.

confidence.rationale: The current helper sets only HTML; the corrected fork builds and its focused Rich Text test passes with both formats.
